description: Single-panel figure that is a data table, not a plot: it tabulates tensile and impact properties, and the caption reproduces the same table plus an "a" footnote. Columns are Steel, UTS/MPa, YS/MPa, UE/%, A/%, Akv-40/J, UTS/MPa^a and FRS/MPa^a; the two superscript-a headers are defined in the caption as sigma_TS, the maximum true stress just before necking (crack nucleation), and the fracture strength. Rows are grouped into three alloy series: Fe30Mn 11Al(x)C (C-0.6, C-1.0, C-1.2, C-1.5), Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C (Mn-20, Mn-25, Mn-30, Mn-35) and Fe30Mn (x)Al1C (Al-6, Al-8, Al-10, Al-11, Al-12). The shared reference composition Fe30Mn-11Al-1C appears three times (C-1.0, Mn-30, Al-11) with identical values (UTS 850 ± 4 MPa, YS 688 ± 2 MPa, UE 62 ± 1.3%, A 70.5 ± 1%, Akv-40 98.0 ± 7.1 J, UTS^a 1343 MPa, FRS^a 2095 MPa). Raising C to 1.5 strongly raises strength but collapses ductility and toughness; higher Al lowers toughness; Mn-35 is the softest grade. No panel labels are printed. All values are mean ± scatter, except the single-value UTS^a and FRS^a columns.

subfigures.description: One table image with header row (Steel, UTS/MPa, YS/MPa, UE/%, A/%, Akv-40/J, UTS/MPa^a, FRS/MPa^a) and 13 data rows in three composition groups; no photographs, curves or micrographs, and no (a)/(b) panel labels.

observations.observation: The image is a single table with no panel labels; its header row reads Steel, UTS/MPa, YS/MPa, UE/%, A/%, Akv-40/J, UTS/MPa^a, FRS/MPa^a.
Rows are grouped under three alloy headings: Fe30Mn 11Al(x)C (C-0.6, C-1.0, C-1.2, C-1.5), Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C (Mn-20, Mn-25, Mn-30, Mn-35) and Fe30Mn (x)Al1C (Al-6, Al-8, Al-10, Al-11, Al-12).
C-1.5 has the highest strength in the table (UTS 1191 ± 1 MPa, YS 1125 ± 1 MPa) but the lowest ductility of the C series (UE 22 ± 1.1%, A 44.0 ± 1%).
C-1.5 also has the lowest FRS^a of the C series (1875 MPa) and an impact energy of only 1.5 ± 0.2 J.
C-1.2 has the lowest impact toughness in its series (Akv-40 2.5 ± 0.2 J) together with the highest FRS^a in the table (2226 MPa).
Al-6 shows the highest impact energy (Akv-40 354 ± 16 J) and highest UTS^a (1410 MPa) of the Fe30Mn (x)Al1C series, and Akv-40 falls monotonically to 3.8 ± 0.1 J at Al-12.
In the Fe(x)Mn 11Al1C series YS falls monotonically from Mn-20 (896 ± 4 MPa) to Mn-35 (401 ± 5 MPa), while total elongation A rises from 66.0 ± 0 to 75.0 ± 1%.

The composition Fe30Mn-11Al-1C appears three times (C-1.0, Mn-30, Al-11) with identical values in every column: UTS 850 ± 4 MPa, YS 688 ± 2 MPa, UE 62 ± 1.3%, A 70.5 ± 1%, Akv-40 98.0 ± 7.1 J, UTS^a 1343 MPa, FRS^a 2095 MPa.

The scatter notation is inconsistent between columns: A/% carries integer deviations (e.g. 74.0 ± 0, 44.0 ± 1) while UTS/MPa and YS/MPa carry one-decimal deviations; the UTS^a and FRS^a columns carry no uncertainty at all.

The caption states that the superscript 'a' on UTS/MPa and FRS/MPa denotes sigma_TS, the maximum true stress just before the onset of necking (crack nucleation during tensile deformation), and the fracture strength, the highest local strength during tensile deformation.
The caption states the mechanical properties were measured after solution-treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h.
The caption states the series covers C from 0.6 to 1.5%, Mn from 20 to 35% and Al from 6.0 to 12.0% in Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels, matching the row labels in the table.

Overall the table shows a strength-versus-ductility/toughness trade-off: the strongest rows (C-1.2, C-1.5, Al-12, Mn-20) are the least tough, and the toughest rows (Al-6, Al-8, Mn-30/C-1.0) have UTS clustered near 830-850 MPa.
